clue.text: Garment disturbing people, put on tearaway's head

indicators.note: one piece is put on top of, in front of, the other in the across entry
the head of the word tearaway is its first letter, the top of it

parts.note: people who disturb or wake others are rousers

explanation.surface: Someone causes a stir by pulling on the trousers of a young tearaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes the first letter T of 'tearaway's'; 'put on' sets it in front of ROUSERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of leg coverings worn from waist to ankle is an everyday item of clothing.

clue.text: Pull rings to dispose of pipes

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so one word goes round the other here

parts.note: to pull hard is to tug
to bin something is to throw it away

explanation.surface: Someone tugs at rings to get rid of some old pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' looks like part of the definition, but the definition is 'pipes' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of hollow cylinder for carrying fluid, collectively, are a material sold by the metre.

clue.text: Musical group starts to offend conductor, tittering every time

indicators.note: the starts of the next five words are their first letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: An orchestra's players upset their conductor by giggling all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letters of 'offend conductor tittering every time'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble of eight players or singers is a small musical group.

clue.text: Fruity concubine?

parts.note: one word names both a dried grape and a woman of a sultan's household, so a concubine might be described as fruity

explanation.surface: A racy mistress is described as fruity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' seems to mean racy or saucy; it really points to a dried grape sharing its name with a sultan's wife or concubine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a seedless raisin and a wife or concubine of a sultan.

clue.text: Luck, of course?

parts.note: on a golf course the putting surface is the green, so chance deflection there is golfing luck; the phrase now means fortune in general

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off good fortune as only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but the course is a golf course: the phrase is golfing slang for a chance bounce of the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a golf term for an accidental deflection of the ball, the phrase now means good or bad fortune.

clue.text: Suffering as a teenager, son a target for infants?

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in family trees
toddlers being toilet-trained aim for a potty

explanation.surface: A parent describes a son's teenage suffering, as if he were a target for small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a target for infants' is the potty used in toilet training.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne commonly afflicts adolescents, leaving the face covered in blemishes or pimples.

clue.text: Bear only odd parts of brash, pompous official

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the famous bear of A. A. Milne's children's books

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word brash, first, third and fifth, are kept

explanation.surface: Someone has to put up with only the odd bits of a brash and pompous official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only odd parts of' keeps letters 1, 3 and 5 of 'brash', giving BAH. The name comes from a self-important character in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Mikado.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandiose holder of many offices, from Gilbert and Sullivan's Mikado, is a byword for a self-important functionary.

clue.text: Curd I spit out of some teeth

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spits curd out from between their teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of CURD, I and SPIT. The definition is an adjective: a tooth with three points is described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Having three cusps or points describes certain molars and premolars, and one heart valve.

clue.text: Surrendering, as soft

definitions.meaning: giving way or handing over to an opponent
giving way under pressure, not firm or rigid

explanation.definitionFit: Giving in to someone is one sense; a material that gives under pressure, being pliant, is another.

clue.text: In which campaigning politicians, needing backing, go round posh area

indicators.note: everything built here is to be read from right to left, backwards
round tells us one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to have a go at something is to have a stab at it
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage
a belt can be a region or zone, as in commuter belt

explanation.surface: Election candidates seeking support tour an affluent district.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion gives SUBELTTAB, which 'needing backing' turns round; 'go round' looks like what the politicians do but splits into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach used by a party's leader and staff to tour the country during an election campaign.

clue.text: Fortunately found doctor in, with spouse tired

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or alter it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A lucky find: a doctor at home, whose husband or wife is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a physician; it is the anagram signal on IN, SPOUSE and TIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming about by happy chance, a discovery made by luck rather than design.

clue.text: For source of oil, all were murdered?

parts.note: if all were murdered, nought would remain alive: the letter O for nought followed by the word live

explanation.surface: A grim question about a massacre over an oil supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the fruit's name as two parts: O, the round figure for nought or none, and LIVE. 'None live' describes a scene in which all were murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Its fruit is pressed to give a cooking oil, so the tree is a source of it.

clue.text: Certainly awful hot inside baked dish when flipped over

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece is placed within the other
a dish flipped over is turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a flan is an open baked tart

indicators.note: awful suggests mangled, so the letters of the word hot are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flips a dish out of the hot oven and it lands upside down, a definite disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' gives OTH and 'flipped over' gives NALF; the phrase is British slang used as an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for very much so, used emphatically to agree with something.

clue.text: Engineers certain to recover

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: Engineers are sure to bounce back after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce back after a setback, regaining strength or value.

clue.text: Briefly successful flambz moment?

definitions.meaning: describes someone or something whose success is short-lived; the phrase is a noun used predicatively
a flambé is set alight in the cooking pan, a brief burst of flame

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from old flintlock guns for a promising start that soon fizzles; cooking a flambé literally makes a burst of fire in a skillet.

clue.text: End of programme about us funny, having shot series?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a programme ends with a fade, the picture or sound dying away
to feel funny is to feel unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A television show ends with us feeling funny after a run of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of programme' looks like a call for a last letter, but it means the fade-out at the close of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid burst of gunfire, many rounds fired together or in quick succession.

clue.text: Due to work out message so can take in information

indicators.note: to work something out is to sort it, here by rearranging the letters of due

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message sent by wire

explanation.surface: Someone has a message to decode so they can absorb the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' rearranges DUE into EDU. The definition is loose: the answer is an adjective, meaning able to take in teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of being taught or trained, so able to absorb knowledge.

clue.text: Uniquely recognised as illustrious

definitions.meaning: told apart from all others, singled out

explanation.definitionFit: Marked out as different from others is one sense; eminent, with a dignified bearing, is the other.

clue.text: Naive girl, popular source of personal information around university

parts.note: something in fashion or popular is described as in

indicators.note: around means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a gene carries the hereditary information unique to each person

explanation.surface: An innocent young woman is a popular source of personal details around campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is from French and is used of an innocent young woman, often a stock theatre role.
explanation.definitionFit: An artless young woman, especially as a stage role, borrowed from French for guileless.

clue.text: Topless prostitute keeps day for something stimulating

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other
topless means its first letter is cut off the top, here in a down entry

parts.note: a whore is a prostitute
Mon is the standard abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: A topless sex worker holds back a day for a bit of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' leaves HORE once the top letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical messenger in the body that triggers activity in organs or tissues, such as adrenaline.

clue.text: Muscle again crushes mushroom

indicators.note: crushes suggests squeezing something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: bis means twice or again, an instruction in music
a cep is an edible wild mushroom, the porcino

explanation.surface: A muscle once again flattens a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is the musical direction for a repeat, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The large muscle at the front of the upper arm, flexed to show strength.

clue.text: Oder said to run into this German city?

definitions.text: Oder said to run into this German city?

parts.words: Oder said to run into this German city?
parts.note: Oder spoken sounds like odour, and a scented water carries the name of this Rhineland city; the river name makes it sound like geography

explanation.surface: A geography question: does the river Oder flow into this German city?
explanation.walkthrough: The Oder is a river, but it never reaches this city, which stands on the Rhine. Said aloud, 'Oder' is odour, and the city gives its name to a perfumed water.
explanation.definitionFit: The city, Köln in German, gave its name to eau de toilette, a fragrance that gives off a scent.

clue.text: One's king returning before one's countryman

indicators.note: before tells us the reversed king comes ahead of the final piece

parts.note: one is I and 's is short for is

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's attaches it to what follows

explanation.surface: Someone's king comes home ahead of a fellow citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LEAR into RAEL. The definition is a citizen of a particular state in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or citizen of a Middle Eastern state founded in 1948, a fellow national.

clue.text: Live figure standing through film

indicators.note: through means one piece passes inside the other

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about a stranded alien

indicators.note: standing means upright, so in a down entry the word reads upwards, in reverse

parts.note: six is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A living figure stands through the whole of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' gives XIS, the number written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alive is to have being, to be present in the world.

clue.text: What page-three girl's missing in intellect?

parts.note: a page-three girl is a topless model in a British tabloid, so the garment she lacks is a bra
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about what a topless model lacks in brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: Page Three was a feature in the British tabloid The Sun showing a topless model.
explanation.definitionFit: The mind or intelligence, the organ of thought standing for mental power.

clue.text: Seeing loo, bursting to find coin

indicators.note: bursting means breaking apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spotting a toilet, desperate to go, finds a coin to pay for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coin' looks like money, but it is the verb, to invent a word. 'bursting' rearranges SEEING and LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a term is to invent new words, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Old boy relinquishing power in English city

parts.note: ex means former, old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: relinquishing means giving up, so a letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Peter is a boy's name
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A former pupil gives up power in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' looks like a former pupil; it is EX plus a boy's name. 'relinquishing' takes P out of PETER. The answer is the county town of Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city that is the county town of Devon in south-west England.

clue.text: Breaking orders for delinquents remains not right — you can't inflame this

indicators.note: breaking into means forcing a way inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: ASBOs were British anti-social behaviour orders, court orders against troublemakers

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: Breaking court orders against young offenders leaves something unrighted, yet you cannot set it alight.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British court order restricting a troublemaker; 'not right' leaves EST.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibrous mineral used for fireproofing, since it does not burn.
